integrator_questions: Did the oval finish rate hold at or above 0.75 at 0.5 kg, and did completion_time improve on the finished runs?
Did line_loss_events fall below 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom with lower mass?
Did steering_oscillation or max_error rise with the lighter mass?
If line loss persists, is the limit wheel-command saturation (+/-4095) or control response?

intent: Restore the iteration-4 geometry (best score 291.9) and change only mass, from 0.6 kg to 0.5 kg, to test whether lower yaw inertia improves turn response on the bends. I kept the span at 50 mm, the forward array at y = 0.075 m, the 12 mm footprint, the 0.12 m track and the 0.12 m body width. I expect the oval to keep or improve its finish rate and the s-bend and slalom line loss to fall. I am considering, without committing, a larger wheel_radius for more speed if the finish time is comfortably under 3 s, but only after the mass result is in. If mass 0.5 kg scores below 291.9, I will return to the exact iteration-4 geometry at 0.6 kg.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) the bend-entry line loss is partly a yaw-inertia limit, so reducing mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg should help the robot turn faster; (2) the oval finish rate is set by stability at speed, so it should hold if mass is not reduced too far; (3) if mass does not clear line loss, the remaining limit is sensor/control rather than geometry, and further geometry search should stop. Measurements requested per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort. completion_time checks whether the lighter robot has speed margin, and line_loss_events separates turn response from sensor coverage.
rationale: The evidence points back to the iteration-4 layout. Iteration 4 (score 291.9) is the only design where the oval finished 15 of 20 runs. Iteration 7 changed only wheel_track to 0.10 m, and the oval finish rate fell to 0 of 20, with max_error at 0.065 to 0.070 and line_loss_events still at 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom. The Integrator's stated rule was to return wheel_track to 0.12 m if the oval finish rate fell or steering_oscillation rose sharply, and both happened, so I am following that advice. I take the Integrator's advice in full on wheel_track and restore 0.12 m. Line loss has now persisted across every span (40 to 60 mm), forward position (0.04 to 0.075 m), footprint (12 and 16 mm) and track (0.10 and 0.12 m) tried so far, and it never cleared. The untested lever is yaw inertia. Yaw inertia = mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, so lowering mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg cuts it by about 17 percent and should give a quicker turn response on the bends without changing the sensor geometry that is working. I change only mass, from the iteration-4 reference, so any change in result can be attributed to mass. Expected result: the oval finish rate should hold at or above 0.75, and line_loss_events and max_error on the s-bend and slalom should improve modestly. Risk: lighter mass can change traction and speed response. If the oval finish rate drops below 0.75 or the score falls below 291.9, the next design should revert to the exact iteration-4 geometry at 0.6 kg, which is the best known.
